articles.title: Amid cold wave, students’ indefinite strike against J&K recruitment board scam gathers steam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Protesting government job aspirants on Saturday (November 21, 2026) launched an indefinite strike in Srinagar amid a cold wave over the government’s failure to act against the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB), the main recruitment agency of J&K that has become mired in a cheating scam that has led to 16 arrests so far.

While former Member of Parliament (MP) Aga Syed Ruhullah joined the protesters in Srinagar, other regional parties also demanded the cancellation of all examinations held by the Board and called for “fixing the responsibility”.

The peaceful sit-in was forcibly broken up by police on Saturday night (November 21), said the protesters. “Students and Aga sahib were removed from the site against their will. The demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA [Finance Accounts Assistant] rigging. This fight isn’t over,” said one protester.
Speaking at the Sher-i-Kashmir Park earlier, Mr. Ruhullah said the protest is a “rare effort to open up space where youth could fight for their rights”.

“We demand that heads must roll. We have the elected government and an unelected government ruling J&K. Both share responsibility for it. Unfortunately, there is a sense of complacency. The examinations should be postponed, responsibility for the irregularities fixed and reforms carried out. The administration should engage students and address their concerns,” said Mr. Ruhullah.

Mr. Ruhullah joined scores of students and aspirants who held a sit-in all day in Srinagar. With evening temperature dipping, a spokesman of Mr. Ruhullah said, “There was no food or blankets. No entry. Students on a peaceful sit-in are being frozen out on a bitter Srinagar night. Their only crime is asking for justice over the alleged Finance Accounts Assistant recruitment rigging.”
The night temperature has dipped to around zero degrees Celsius in Srinagar amid a severe cold wave.
On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts.

Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. Besides 16 arrests made in the case, the police said it filed three First Information Reports (FIRs) and recovered eight wireless devices, 22 mobile phones and four vehicles of the accused.

However, Board chairman Shrikant Balasaheb Suse said the “examination was not compromised by a paper leak or mass malpractice” and announced that the upcoming exams will be held “as per the schedule”.
Facing a growing public outcry, J&K Education Minister Shamim Firdous said strict action should be taken “if any irregularities or rigging are found”.
“Students, who have worked hard, deserve justice. We have already ordered an inquiry to identify the irregularities, and action will follow if evidence is found,” said Ms. Firdous.

articles.title: Vasan urges political parties to fight for Cauvery water rights
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Saturday urged the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) to direct the Karnataka government to release water due to Tamil Nadu. He also sought the cooperation of political parties in Tamil Nadu in securing the State’s rights by setting aside their differences.
In a statement, Mr. Vasan expressed shock over the Supreme Court dismissing Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking the release of 11 thousand million cubic feet of Cauvery water by Karnataka.
He said that, in the past, the Karnataka government had not complied with the directions of the CWMA and had acted in a step-motherly manner.

Farmers in the Cauvery delta are under severe economic distress due to an acute shortage of water for irrigation. The Karnataka government should understand that the Cauvery water-sharing issue and the Mekedatu issue are not only river water disputes, but also the lifelines of the people of Tamil Nadu, Mr. Vasan added.

articles.title: Municipal staff transfers to move online by Tamil Nadu govt., with vacancies displayed on portal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Tamil Nadu government has introduced online counselling for transfers and postings of employees in municipal corporations, municipal councils and town panchayats, covering employees in the lower and middle levels of the government pay structure, including posts such as assistants, junior assistants and superintendents. The guidelines were issued through two Government Orders (G.O.s) by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department dated November 19, 2026.
The counselling will be based on vacancies and station seniority. The online portal is being developed by the respective heads of departments and will be introduced shortly, an official said.

Regarding whether employees would be able to raise grievances relating to seniority or other issues through the portal, the official said the department would be asked to incorporate a provision for submitting representations online. The portal would also provide details of vacancies and the procedure for applying for transfers, he said.

According to the guidelines, general transfers will ordinarily be conducted between April 1 and May 31 every year. Applications will be received through the online portal between March 1 and 31. Employees who have completed three years of service in a post or station will be liable for transfer during this period, subject to the availability of vacancies.

Transfers during the non-transfer period, between June 1 and March 31, will be permitted only on administrative grounds, including promotions, disciplinary reasons, complaints, long leave arrangements and other administrative exigencies.

All transfers, including those sought by employees, during the transfer period will be processed through the online portal. The guidelines also provide for a maximum of three alternative station preferences in transfer applications.
The official said counselling for Executive Officers of town panchayats had already been conducted and postings issued based on it.

articles.title: AIPC Tamil Nadu to support MSMEs through professional network
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Tamil Nadu chapter should function as a professional support network for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), helping them access legal, financial and technical expertise, said its national chairman Madhu Goud Yaskhi at the organisation’s annual summit in Chennai on Saturday.

Mr. Yaskhi proposed that chartered accountants, lawyers, engineers and IT professionals associated with the AIPC volunteer their time to help MSMEs with taxation, regulatory compliance, financial management and delayed payments.

He said over ₹7 lakh crore owed to small enterprises across India remained stuck in delayed payments, with large companies often taking more than 120 days to clear dues despite the statutory 45-day limit.

The AIPC could also take up delayed payments by State public sector undertakings with the Tamil Nadu government, he said. Lawyers could help MSMEs pursue their dues through legal notices, while chartered accountants could assist with invoice discounting and compliance.
Outgoing AIPC chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty said Congress needed to reconnect with professionals in major urban centres, where it had lost electoral ground since 2014, he said.

He also urged professionals to help implement and promote the Tamil Nadu government’s policies, including the Private University Bill, startup initiatives and tourism projects, saying the Congress’s participation in the coalition government brought responsibilities beyond its share in the Cabinet.
After the event, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan told reporters that the Private University Bill passed by the Assembly had received the Governor’s assent.

The government would prepare a standard operating procedure and issue guidelines for its implementation, he said. The legislation aimed to attract foreign universities to Tamil Nadu and provide students access to international-standard educational facilities within the State.
Lok Sabha MP C. Robert Bruce and Rajya Sabha MP Christopher Tilak were present.

articles.title: Gandhi is the core ideological enemy of the Sangh Parivar: Ramachandra Guha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: While early years after Independence in India saw excessive veneration of Gandhi, the recent trends have shifted to a “venomous detestation” of the man by the right-wing ecosystem led by the Sangh Parivar, historian Ramachandra Guha said here on Saturday while discussing his latest book Arguments with Gandhi.

“When I was young, the ethos in India was excessive veneration of Gandhi. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. That should be very evident from whatever they say about Gandhi. Actually, Gandhi is their core ideological enemy, as he has once been of the Left.” Dr. Guha averred. Citing an analogy, he said that Prime Minister Modi, in his article on Gandhi in the New York Times on his 150th birth anniversary, “praised him for everything except Hindu-Muslim harmony”. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan.

Elaborating on the reasons for such attacks on Gandhi, Dr. Guha emphasised that Gandhi had come to represent the feminine in the eyes of the “macho Right”, what with his non-violent policy, inter-faith harmony, his scepticism of the State, or his scepticism of progress.

“Gandhi raises almost all the important questions of human existence today. You can think of no other thinker; he catches so many vital aspects of our lives,” Dr. Guha observed, as the conversation veered towards his ideas of non-violent science which influenced several scientists, including J.B.S. Haldane and Laurie Baker. Gandhi, he said, derived his principles from all traditions and belief systems – Jainism, Vaishnavism, Christianity, and even communism. His attitude to gender, religion, or non-violence evolved through his engagements with various philosophies.

“I do not see him as a quintessentially Hindu thinker, quintessentially Indian thinker, [or] quintessentially traditional thinker. He transcends these lanes. Or Leftist, Rightist, Conservative; he is all three,” Dr. Guha added.

On the question of caste and the equations with the Ambedkarite principles, Dr. Guha said that Gandhi was a guilt-ridden upper caste while Ambedkar was a dalit without emancipation and they could only take those paths. From the perspective of history and the future of India, the paths are converging. Asked if Gandhi’s methods are lost in the era of social media, he said the “cockroaches showed that they have it”. If the book came out a few months later, he said he would have added a few paragraphs on the Cockroach Janata Party movement.

articles.title: T.N. may see solar energy installations slowing down, say energy generators
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu, which has 10,000 MW-11,000 MW of installed solar energy capacity, may see a slowdown in solar energy installations in 2027, according to industry representatives.

The single window system for obtaining approvals is not functioning effectively, finer details based on the recently-announced Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy should be notified by the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, and costs are escalating, say solar energy investors.

“No approvals have been granted for solar energy projects for almost six months now. Only now has the government started accepting the applications. Even if they are approved now, it is difficult to commission the projects by March 2027. From April next year, it is mandatory for all new projects to have BESS, and this will push the costs up,” said one of the solar energy investors in Coimbatore.

“We had a detailed discussion with the TNERC on the BESS policy. The policy says there will be waiver of wheeling charges. The wheeling charges are applicable only if a consumer buys under open access. However, the policy says solar energy generators who store energy can sell it only to the State utility. There are many such issues with the policy that need better clarity in the policy ,” says AD Thirumoorthy, State Level Renewable Energy Committee Member, Government of Tamil Nadu.

The single window approval system is functioning effectively for solar energy projects that come as a part of foreign direct investments. The others require multiple approvals, starting right from the rural local body heads. These lead to delays, pushing up the costs, he added.

While the BESS policy is a welcome move, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation should ensure that stored solar energy is evacuated within 24 hours, so that the generator can store freshly generated energy the next day, said L. Santhosh, president of the Tamil Nadu Electricity Consumers Association.

In the last one month, some of the solar energy generators received notices demanding 8% banking charges. These are not applicable because the court has stayed the green energy open access policy of the State, he added. More sub-stations and solutions for right of way challenges to lay lines on lands belonging to various government departments are among the other issues faced by investors that threaten to slow down solar energy projects.

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: “India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

Bilateral trade in goods and services between India and Finland stood at around $3.7 billion in 2025-26, marking a growth of about 25% over the previous year, and a 38.5% rise from $2.64 billion in 2021-22.
The startup event, Polar Bear Pitching, originated in Oulu, northern Finland, and has expanded internationally, connecting startups with investors and business networks.

articles.title: What does EPFO’s Systematic Withdrawal Plan entail for retirees | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Story So Far: The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), in a meeting held in New Delhi on November 19, 2026 approved the Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for EPF members, enabling periodic payouts of retirement savings. As per the proposed SWP, upon retirement or superannuation, a member will have several options to receive the accumulated PF corpus or a part through periodic withdrawals instead of a lump-sum withdrawal.

As of now, a retiring PF subscriber generally withdraws the entire provident fund accumulation as a lump sum. The proposal, cleared by the CBT, say an eligible member, upon retirement, may opt to receive their provident fund accumulations as monthly withdrawals; quarterly withdrawals; half-yearly withdrawals; or annual withdrawals. The remaining corpus will be invested within the EPF Fund and will continue to earn EPF interest on the running balance. The SWP scheme also proposes to provide flexible options to the member for enhancing his or her corpus in PF by voluntary contributions through payroll, direct additional contributions other than payroll and third-party micro-contributions.

articles.title: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Growth in the core industrial sectors of the economy climbed to a series-high of 10.9% in October 2026, driven by a surge in electricity generation, and coal, cement, and iron ore production, and a low base effect, official data released on Friday (November 20, 2026) showed.

Data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on the Index of Core Industries shows that growth in October surpassed the 8.2% in September, the previous series high. The new index, released this year with a base year of 2022-23, has data that goes back only up to April 2024.
However, the data also shows that the strong growth figure in October was also likely aided by the fact that the index grew a relatively poor 0.8% in October last year.

“While core output surged by 10.9% in October 2026, the fastest pace in the new series, this was supported by a low base related to the shift in the festive calendar, with output having expanded by a marginal 0.8% in the year ago month,” Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA said.

“While the growth print for October 2026 signals a strong start for the third quarter of FY2027, this is largely optical,” Ms. Nayar added. “The average performance for October-November 2026 would provide a better assessment, as this would adjust for festive base effects.”

Within the index, the coal sector saw growth accelerating to 23.05% in October 2026, far faster than the 10.7% registered in September. October’s performance, however, is likely also due to low base effect, since the sector contracted 8.4% in October last year.

The growth in the index, however, is in line with what the industry itself has reported. Coal India, the country’s largest coal company, reported that production increased about 19% to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October.

A major reason for the growth in coal production was likely demand from the power sector, which saw electricity generation jump by 21.6% in October 2026, up from 12.6% in the previous month. However, this sector too could have benefited from a low base effect, since it contracted nearly 7% in October 2025.
Within the index, the infrastructure-related sectors were the only ones that grew strongly without the aid of a statistical low base effect.

The iron ore sector, for example, grew at a three-month high of 23.4% in October 2026, compared to 18.4% in September and 8.7% in October last year. One of the factors driving this strong growth was that steel production grew at 7.3% in October, the fastest rate in seven months.
The cement sector also grew at a series-high of 15.4% in October 2026, compared to 10.1% in September, and 5.2% in October last year.
The fuel-related sectors in the Index other than coal continued to perform relatively poorly.

articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.
The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.
Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

articles.title: CEA flags need to align capital markets with India’s development priorities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has called for a greater role for Indian capital markets in channelising household savings into productive investments, stressing the importance of patient capital in meeting the country’s long-term development needs.

Speaking at the CII Financial Summit in Mumbai, Mr. Nageswaran said sectors such as infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture and mineral exploration required long-term financing, given their extended investment horizons.
Highlighting the imbalance in India’s financial markets, he pointed out that equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

While acknowledging that technology had improved market access, settlement systems and transaction security, he said these advances had not necessarily translated into better outcomes for investors or the real economy.

“A safer machine is not the same as a better outcome,” he said, emphasising that technological innovation should ultimately strengthen the capital market’s core function of converting savings into productive investments.
Cautioning against a consumption-led economic model, Mr. Nageswaran said, “An economy that is consumption-oriented may not be the most suited one for India’s development context.”

Echoing the need to promote long-term savings, Gaurav Mathur, founder and managing director of SafeGold, called for tax incentives to encourage investors to hold financial assets for longer periods. He stressed that savings policies should reflect individuals’ financial circumstances and different stages of life.

“It’s a matter of constructive partnership between regulators and financial intermediaries, where you incentivise long-term saving behaviour at the appropriate stages in life,” Mr. Mathur said, adding that incentives should particularly target wealthier individuals with greater capacity to save.

Meanwhile, Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company and part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, underscored the need to strengthen financial literacy and encourage voluntary pension savings. He said these measures were increasingly important amid uncertainties over employment and income in a technology-driven economy.

articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline.

One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a).

Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. What he did not explain though was why and where did this labour productivity rise come from. Much later, his successors argued that the growth of labour productivity depends on investment in human capital, research and development, patent regimes, etc., what came to be known as endogenous growth theories.

articles.title: The Rohingya | Vindication for a persecuted people
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: In a first of a kind ruling, the International Court of Justice held on November 19 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State during the military’s “clearance operations” in 2017. This was the first time the ICJ found a state responsible for committing genocide. Nine judges against six voted in favour of the ruling, in a case brought in 2019 by The Gambia.

The court also found that Myanmar failed to prevent genocide by civilians who joined its forces, failed to punish the perpetrators, never enacted the laws that the Genocide Convention requires, and destroyed evidence in breach of the court’s 2020 interim order. It also rejected, by 14 votes to one, the charge that Myanmar directly and publicly incited private persons to commit genocide, but declined to order citizenship for the Rohingya.

The judgment holds the state of Myanmar to account but does not convict any individual. It is final and cannot be appealed. The court ordered Myanmar to investigate and, if warranted, prosecute those responsible, guarantee that the violations will not recur, allow the “safe, voluntary and dignified” return of the displaced, restore their property and compensate the Rohingya. The amount of compensation is to be fixed later, after Myanmar reports back to the court within two years.

The Rohingya are a predominantly Muslim people who speak an Indo-Aryan language close to the Chittagonian dialect. The 2014 Census in Myanmar estimated over a million Rohingya in the country, concentrated in Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung along the Bangladesh border. Muslims have lived in Rakhine or Arakan from the time of the Mrauk U kingdom (15th to 18th century). In 1799, the British physician Francis Buchanan recorded that Muslims “long settled in Arakan” called themselves the “Rooinga”.

Many joined them, coming from Chittagong during colonial rule. Historian Jacques Leider has said the “Rohingya” took on a political and ethnic meaning in the late 1950s, when Muslim leaders adopted it to claim the status of a “national race”. In 1961, Brig. Aung Gyi of the Burmese Army publicly accepted them as an ethnic group. But this was before the coup by General Ne Win in 1962 which heralded decades of rule by the military junta in the country.

articles.title: Iran wants diplomacy to end war, says Araghchi as U.S. rejects terms
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran still hoped diplomacy could end its war with the United States, while U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but one that was not acceptable to him.

Mr. Araghchi told the state-owned Iran newspaper that Tehran was seeking “an agreement that would ensure there was no further war” and wanted guarantees that Washington was serious about negotiations before proceeding further, adding that Iran had discussed with mediators the form and nature of confidence-building measures.

The remarks came as diplomatic efforts continued to try to end a conflict that has destabilised the West Asia, disrupted shipping, driven up global energy prices and drawn in countries across the region.
The Foreign Minister said Iran’s red lines included keeping enriched uranium in the country, though he added that he believed “a fair solution” could be reached.
“They want to make a deal, but they don’t want to make a deal that’s acceptable to me,” Mr. Trump said at a press conference on Friday.
The United States and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to strike Israel and Gulf states hosting U.S. military bases.

Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) in talks aimed at “bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals presented on the ground,” a spokesperson for Qatar’s Foreign Ministry said.

U.S. Central Command on Saturday (November 20, 2026) denied an Iranian account that its forces had fired a missile at a U.S. F-16 fighter jet over the Gulf, damaging the aircraft and forcing it to make an emergency landing.
Iranian state media earlier reported that the country’s air defence systems targeted the aircraft on Friday evening, causing it to abort its mission and land at a nearby airport.
“Iran did not attack a US F-16 fighter aircraft yesterday — at all,” Central Command said in a statement.

articles.title: Sri Lanka's organised crime bill gets Supreme Court nod
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Sri Lanka's proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill has received the Supreme Court's nod, which ruled that its provisions are "not inconsistent" with the Constitution, Speaker Jagath Wickremaratna told Parliament on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

The Bill, tabled in Parliament on October 20, has drawn criticism from local and international rights groups concerned that its provisions could undermine fundamental rights and grant sweeping powers to law enforcement agencies.

In Sri Lanka, citizens can challenge a Bill's constitutionality in the Supreme Court within one week of its introduction in Parliament. The Bill had earlier faced 20 petitions in the Supreme Court challenging its constitutionality.
The Speaker on Saturday (November 21, 2026) confirmed the Supreme Court's nod for the Bill and listed the clauses it directed Parliament to amend.

"The clauses in the Bill are not inconsistent with the Constitution and may be passed by a simple majority of Parliament, subject to making the amendment at the committee stage," Mr. Wickremaratna said.
He said Clause 6, which allowed the prosecution of an individual who is not a member of a criminal gang, should be deleted, citing the Court's directions.

Criticism of the Bill has centred on its broad definition of organised crime and provisions that could allow authorities to identify individuals as gang members based on their appearance or associations.

Sri Lanka's Human Rights Commission called for the Bill's withdrawal, while the Bar Association of Sri Lanka raised concerns about its impact on fundamental rights and safeguards for judicial oversight.

Rights body Amnesty International also called for its complete withdrawal, while the New York-based Human Rights Watch said the proposed legislation fell short of international human rights standards.

Rights groups have also raised concerns over extended detention, the admissibility of confessions made to senior police officers, restrictions on bail, police surveillance and searches and arrests without warrants.
Other contentious provisions relate to media freedom and the scope of police powers, critics have said.

articles.title: Yemen's Houthis launch strikes after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Yemen's Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday (November 21, 2026), after vowing reprisals for a "special operation" by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them.

Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was "under a hostile aerial threat".
The coalition later said it had "intercepted and destroyed" three Houthi ballistic missiles headed for the capital.
The Iran-backed Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh.
The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on Friday (November 20, 2026).
The "special operation" hit smuggling and weapons-transporting operations in Hodeida, the coalition said.
It also involved attacks on Sanaa, Saada and Taiz governorates, marking an uptick in violence after months of hostilities.

The Houthis had vowed to hit the Saudi city of Jeddah and other Red Sea ports if Hodeida was attacked, while warning airlines that Saudi airspace was "unsafe". The group also threatened Riyadh's financial district and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said its forces had "targeted operational capabilities at Hodeida port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles".
The coalition also hit "military targets" in Sanaa, including missile and drone facilities and a supply depot, he said on X.

The Houthis said coalition strikes had killed 41 people in the previous 24 hours. Yemen's Saudi-backed armed forces said dozens of airstrikes and drone attacks, as well as hundreds of artillery attacks, killed or wounded 193 Houthi fighters.

articles.title: Israeli strike kills three in vehicle distributing aid in Gaza, witnesses say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: An Israeli strike killed three Palestinians ​in a vehicle carrying papers and food for the World ⁠Central Kitchen charity in Gaza City on Saturday (November 21, 2026), Gaza's Health Ministry and witnesses said.
World Central Kitchen, an aid organisation that distributes food in the Gaza Strip, said, however, ‌that the vehicle was not affiliated with it.

The Israeli military said several militants had been targeted in the area without providing ‌further details. It did not immediately respond to questions on why ‌it ⁠had hit a vehicle that appeared to be distributing aid.
A ⁠Reuters witness said the vehicle appeared to be carrying packaged foodstuffs, and that papers inside carried World Central Kitchen's logo.
"It was just about to stop to distribute the food and ​drink to children when it was ‌hit by a missile," said Abu Zein Al-Daya, who witnessed the strike.
Afterwards, meals of cooked rice were scattered around the vehicle, which was partially covered in the blood of the victims of the attack.
The Israeli military killed seven World Central Kitchen workers ​in a 2024 strike, including citizens of Australia, Britain and Poland.
At the time, the military said there had been "serious errors and ⁠breaches of procedure" but in 2026 it said it had found no basis on which to open criminal investigations into the incident.
Israel briefly launched a ‌ground operation in Gaza earlier this week and killed six people in a strike on a hospital that it said was targeting a commander for the Palestinian militant group Hamas.
An October 2025 U.S.-backed ceasefire halted major fighting in the shattered territory but has not stopped Israeli attacks on Gaza or secured Hamas' disarmament.
At least 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers have been ‌killed since then, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.
Israeli troops now control around ​two-thirds of Gaza, up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, with Hamas controlling a sliver of territory ⁠along Gaza's coast.

articles.title: Cargo ship bound for Russia's Kaliningrad hit by drones, Finland tightens security
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A cargo ship bound for Russia's Baltic exclave ‌of Kaliningrad was struck by drones in international waters in ​the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, Russian and Finnish authorities ⁠said, prompting Finland to tighten security measures in the area.

The vessel was damaged west of Russia's Gogland island, caught fire and later drifted into Finnish territorial waters, Finland's Defence ‌Forces said, corroborating an earlier account by Russian officials.

Leningrad region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said the vessel had been attacked by two ‌drones in international waters about three nautical miles from Russia's border. ‌The ⁠crew was being evacuated and the extent of the damage ⁠was being assessed, he said.

Finland's Defence Ministry said the military had reintroduced temporary aviation and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland as a precaution to protect civilians and enable authorities ​to operate if drones needed ‌to be intercepted.
Finland had informed its allies about the incident, the ministry said.

Estonia's Police and Border Guard Board said in an emailed statement it had been informed that a fire had broken out aboard the Russian ‌cargo vessel Sparta II and that preliminary information indicated there had ​been explosions on board.

"The war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas. Finnish ⁠authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to ‌fight against the aggressor," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said on X.

"The situation poses no danger to other maritime traffic... Preparations for potential rescue operations are being made in cooperation with other authorities in Finland and internationally," the Finnish Border Guard said in a statement.
Drozdenko also said 80 drones had been shot down over the Leningrad region and lifted a drone ‌threat warning.
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said on X his country was monitoring the ​situation and had offered help to its neighbour Finland, without giving details.
Ukraine's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request ⁠for comment.
Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said the incident posed no threat to supplies ⁠to the region.

articles.title: COP31 extends into overtime in Turkiye meeting
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Much like the 1.5 degree Celsius warming ceiling, COP31 proceedings under way at Antalya in Turkiye also breached upper limits with countries, as of Saturday (November 21, 2026) evening, yet to behold a final text or convene a final plenary meeting to decide on the path forward for climate action.

Proceedings were expected to officially conclude on Friday (November 20, 2026), though historically it almost always goes into overtime and extends into the early hours of the weekend. The inability to reach a compromise — every clause of the final text must be agreed upon by every participating country — is due to the familiar division between a bloc of European countries and developing countries over a timeline to phase out fossil fuels and defining and paying out the trillions of dollars necessary to fund that transition as well as adapt to ongoing climate change.

The latest public iteration of the COP31 draft cover text, as of November 19, has eliminated references to fossil fuels phase out and net zero dates but has also deleted references to a firm US $120 billion adaptation-finance target that developing countries have been asking for as “legally binding financial obligations” on developed countries.

Taking off from the previous editions of the COP in Baku, Azerbaijan and Belem, Brazil, developed nations said they would “take the lead” in contributing at least $300 billion annually towards mitigation and adaptation to climate change by 2035, though developing countries say this should be at least $ 1.3 trillion.

Other than the thorny debate on whether loans, grants, and for-profit investments in green projects are all included in this number, there is also debate on how much of the annual money should be split between adaptation and mitigation. The $120 billion was a proposal but that now has disappeared from the latest version of the text.
This suggests that the most ambitious demands of both the developed and developing country blocs have been eliminated.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome it needs the consensus of all Parties. The Presidency has said earlier drafts were not meant to reflect consensus.

However, a widely expected outcome of raising electricity’s share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035 and scaling up the use of carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS) technologies. The latter involves unproven, expensive technology to extract atmospheric carbon dioxide. Proponents say this is necessary to counter the effects of the carbon that’s already in the atmosphere and responsible for the 1.5C temperature breach that has already occurred. To reiterate, the Paris Agreement goal is to keep temperatures below 2C and “as far as possible” below 1.5C. However, this has also been criticised by several civil society organisations as being an excuse to delay fossil-fuel phaseout.

“CC[U]S has been researched and developed for decades yet has achieved no discernible breakthroughs in efficiency, capture rates, or costs. Indeed, costs are getting higher. CCS is a tax on energy supplies at a time when affordability is strained and demand growth is seeking efficient supplies,” said Grant Hauber, Strategic Energy Finance Advisor, Asia, Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) in a statement,” CO2 capture and disposal are a pure cost to the energy and production system.”

“We’re down to the wire at COP31, and the latest texts are alarmingly far from ambitious or equitable,” said Rachel Cleetus, Climate Program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS), in a statement. “ Rich nations, most notably the EU nations, are still holding a harsh line against committing to tripling adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035. Instead of reaching agreement on urgently needed climate finance, some countries seem willing to push negotiations toward failure.”

“The attempt to prove that a flashy headline target signals success for this COP has gone wrong in many ways for this Presidency,” said Avantika Goswami, Programme Manager, Centre for Science and Environment. “This text is a messy collation of disparate targets, some proposed as a menu of options, and some new decisions to establish new agendas. It lacks coherence and vision.”

articles.title: HPV vaccination: one crore doses administered in nine months
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: India has administered more than one crore doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in less than nine months, covering nearly 87% of its annual target cohort of 14-year-old girls under the national cervical cancer prevention campaign launched in February 2026, noted a release issued by the Union Health Ministry on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

It added that Uttar Pradesh leads with more than 29.33 lakh girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar (13.70 lakh) and Gujarat (7.75 lakh). Six States — Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar — have achieved 100% coverage of their identified target populations.

The government provides the single-dose vaccine free of cost and voluntarily to eligible girls at designated government health facilities, with parental consent. The U-WIN digital platform facilitates beneficiary tracking, real-time monitoring, slot booking and digital certificates. Vaccination sessions are conducted under medical supervision, with arrangements for managing adverse events following immunisation, the Ministry said.
Among other high-performing States, Assam has recorded 95.63% coverage, followed by Telangana (95.28%), Karnataka (93.16%) and Uttarakhand (90.17%).

Chhattisgarh (86.21%) and Rajasthan (85.23%) have crossed the 80% coverage mark, while Kerala (77.02%), Tamil Nadu (76.12%), Odisha (74.90%) and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (72.99%) have achieved more than 70% coverage.

In terms of absolute numbers, Uttar Pradesh leads the country with more than 29.33 lakh 14-year-old girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar with more than 13.70 lakh and Gujarat with more than 7.75 lakh girls vaccinated.

“School teachers, Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs) and other frontline healthcare workers have worked closely with parents and communities to encourage informed participation and counter misinformation,’’ the Ministry added.

It stated that digital health infrastructure has been an important enabler of the nationwide campaign, with the U-WIN platform supporting real-time monitoring, beneficiary tracking and digital vaccination records.

The platform also enables parents to book HPV vaccination slots for their daughters and download digital vaccination certificates, making the vaccination process more accessible, convenient and transparent.

articles.title: At least 13 dead after consuming spurious liquor, over 300 hospitalised in Manipur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: At least 13 people have died, and more than 300 have been hospitalised since November 18 after they consumed spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel district, police said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
The patients are mostly from Chakpikarong and surrounding areas and have been hospitalised across multiple healthcare facilities in Imphal, including JNIMS, RIMS, Shija and Babina Hospital.

"Thirteen people have been reported dead till 9 p.m. on Friday, while 346 patients have been admitted to hospitals due to suspected methanol poisoning, as they consumed spurious liquor," an official told PTI .
Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited Shija Hospital and Babina Hospital on Friday afternoon (November 20, 2026) to assess the situation and meet patients undergoing treatment.

In a social media post, Mr. Singh said, "Visited Shija Hospital at Lamphelpat, and Babina Hospital at Sajiwa, today [on Friday] to enquire about the health condition of the persons undergoing treatment after consuming spurious liquor from Chakpikarong area in Chandel District."
The Chandel district administration has intensified emergency response measures, and a team has been constituted for coordinated monitoring of the situation, an official notification said.
Four rapid response teams, equipped with adequate medicines and oxygen supplies, have been deployed in the district, the official said.

"Over 140 patients were admitted to Shija Hospital and over 41 patients at Babina Hospital. The death toll has touched 11 during the last 48 hours. The patients are undergoing medical evaluation and treatment under the close supervision of the doctors," he said.

"A medical team, led by a Specialist in General Medicine, along with essential medicines, has left for Chandel District to strengthen on-ground treatment and response", he said adding, "The government will conduct an enquiry and the culprits will be punished."
Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan .K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications.
"Some patients are also undergoing hemodialysis", he added.
A JNIMS doctor said, "Many of the hospitalised include individuals who had consumed local liquor and had come to the hospital due to fear."

articles.title: Study highlights need for trauma-informed, community-based mental health support for refugees in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Mental health concerns among refugee communities are linked not only to past trauma, violence and forced displacement but also to legal uncertainty, limited work opportunities, poor living conditions and social isolation in host countries, finds a study of Sri Lankan Tamil and Rohingya communities in India, published in the International Journal of Migration, Health and Social Care.

Titled ‘Building mental health capacity in protracted refugee situations: Empirical pointers from Sri Lankan Tamil and Rohingya populations in India’, the study looks at common mental health concerns and barriers to accessing care. It calls for training community members and health workers to recognise psychological distress, provide basic support and facilitate access to professional mental health services.

articles.title: South Korea confirms first case of cholera in 10 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: South Korea on Friday reported its first case of cholera in 10 years, with health authorities urging people to take precautionary measures, use only safe water and wash their food properly.

The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency said health workers confirmed cholera from test samples of a person who had visited a hospital emergency room in the southeastern port city of Changwon earlier this month, showing symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea.

The agency said the unidentified person, who recovered and was discharged on Tuesday, had not travelled overseas in the past two months. It said health workers were trying to trace the source of infection and the people the person had been in contact with.

It was the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001.

The agency issued guidance urging people to stick to safe water and cooked food and to wash and peel fruits and vegetables. It also urged medical facilities to promptly test and report suspected cases.

articles.title: Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in DR Congo next week: WHO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Two potential vaccines against the deadly Ebola strain gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo are set to enter trials in the outbreak's epicentre next week, the World Health Organisation announced earlier this week.
There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the explosive outbreak declared in May, triggering an international public health emergency.
A total of 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO.

"We expect two candidate vaccines developed specifically for Bundibugyo virus to begin testing as early as next week," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told a press conference at the UN health agency's headquarters in Geneva.

The so-called Tumaini trial in the DRC is a single framework that can test the safety, efficacy and ability to trigger an immune response of multiple vaccines. The trial uses ring vaccination: immunising contacts deemed to be at high risk of infection.

Ervebo, a vaccine already approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, kicked off the Tumaini trial on October 23, at the full-scale Phase 3 level, to determine if it also offers any protection against Bundibugyo.
The trial will now also incorporate the two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which have both gone through earlier-stage, smaller-scale Phase 1 clinical trials.

One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab developed by the University of Oxford; the other, mRNA-1469, was developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Meg Doherty, head of the WHO's science for health department, said Phase 2 clinical trials with the candidate vaccines are scheduled to begin on November 26 or 27 in Bunia, the capital of the DRC's northeastern Ituri province at the epicentre of the outbreak.
If the safety and immune response data from the Phase 2 trial pass the next stage of review, the candidate jabs can move forward to a full-scale Phase 3 trial.

Doherty said that more than 140 people were enrolled in the Tumaini trial, with thousands of contacts ultimately expected to sign up. The trial will also eventually expand beyond the current single site in Bunia.
Ebola, which spreads through contact with bodily fluids and causes a haemorrhagic fever, has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. But much will depend on what follows.

Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.title: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

articles.title: Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.

That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. articles.title: Amid cold wave, students’ indefinite strike against J&K recruitment board scam gathers steam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Protesting government job aspirants on Saturday (November 21, 2026) launched an indefinite strike in Srinagar amid a cold wave over the government’s failure to act against the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB), the main recruitment agency of J&K that has become mired in a cheating scam that has led to 16 arrests so far.

While former Member of Parliament (MP) Aga Syed Ruhullah joined the protesters in Srinagar, other regional parties also demanded the cancellation of all examinations held by the Board and called for “fixing the responsibility”.

The peaceful sit-in was forcibly broken up by police on Saturday night (November 21), said the protesters. “Students and Aga sahib were removed from the site against their will. The demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA [Finance Accounts Assistant] rigging. This fight isn’t over,” said one protester.
Speaking at the Sher-i-Kashmir Park earlier, Mr. Ruhullah said the protest is a “rare effort to open up space where youth could fight for their rights”.

“We demand that heads must roll. We have the elected government and an unelected government ruling J&K. Both share responsibility for it. Unfortunately, there is a sense of complacency. The examinations should be postponed, responsibility for the irregularities fixed and reforms carried out. The administration should engage students and address their concerns,” said Mr. Ruhullah.

Mr. Ruhullah joined scores of students and aspirants who held a sit-in all day in Srinagar. With evening temperature dipping, a spokesman of Mr. Ruhullah said, “There was no food or blankets. No entry. Students on a peaceful sit-in are being frozen out on a bitter Srinagar night. Their only crime is asking for justice over the alleged Finance Accounts Assistant recruitment rigging.”
The night temperature has dipped to around zero degrees Celsius in Srinagar amid a severe cold wave.
On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts.

Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. Besides 16 arrests made in the case, the police said it filed three First Information Reports (FIRs) and recovered eight wireless devices, 22 mobile phones and four vehicles of the accused.

However, Board chairman Shrikant Balasaheb Suse said the “examination was not compromised by a paper leak or mass malpractice” and announced that the upcoming exams will be held “as per the schedule”.
Facing a growing public outcry, J&K Education Minister Shamim Firdous said strict action should be taken “if any irregularities or rigging are found”.
“Students, who have worked hard, deserve justice. We have already ordered an inquiry to identify the irregularities, and action will follow if evidence is found,” said Ms. Firdous.
